entities.summary:
Wells Fargo & Company is an American multinational financial services company founded in 1852 in San Francisco by Henry Wells and William Fargo to serve gold rush California. Now one of the 'Big Four' US banks, it serves over 70 million customers and operates the largest US bank branch network.

Wells Fargo became iconic in the American West through its stagecoach network delivering mail, gold, and passengers across frontier territories. The original express company merged with American Express before the banking operations expanded. During the 20th century, Wells Fargo grew into a major California bank and acquired Crocker Bank (1986) and First Interstate Bancorp (1996). Norwest Corporation's 1998 merger created the nationwide bank headquartered in San Francisco.

The 2008 acquisition of Wachovia during the financial crisis created a true coast-to-coast banking giant, but Wells Fargo became embroiled in the most serious consumer fraud scandal in US banking history: from 2002 to 2016, employees opened over 3.5 million fake accounts without customer consent to meet sales quotas, resulting in $3 billion in fines and comprehensive regulatory restrictions. The scandal revealed systemic incentive problems in retail banking and triggered major industry reforms.
